record.context_brief: Low-regularity invariant curves for twist maps
record.original_question: For each regularity level r∈[1,∞]∪{analytic}, does there exist a C^r area-preserving twist map with a rotational invariant curve that is not C^1?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.1.1 (J. Mather) Does there exist an example of a cr twist area­ preserving map with a rotational invariant curve which is not C1 (sepamte question fo each r E [1,00] U {w}).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{A} = \mathbb{T} \times \mathbb{R}$ denote the closed (or open) annulus with coordinates $(\theta, r)$, equipped with the standard area form $d\theta \wedge dr$. A diffeomorphism $f: \mathbb{A} \to \mathbb{A}$ of class $C^r$ is called an area-preserving twist map if it preserves $d\theta \wedge dr$, preserves orientation and the two ends of the annulus, and satisfies the twist condition $\partial \theta_1 / \partial r > 0$, where $(\theta_1, r_1) = f(\theta, r)$ (with $\theta_1$ taken as a lift to $\mathbb{R}$). A rotational (essential) invariant curve for $f$ is a homotopically nontrivial simple closed curve $\Gamma \subset \mathbb{A}$ with $f(\Gamma) = \Gamma$; by Birkhoff's theorem, every such curve is the graph of a Lipschitz function $\psi: \mathbb{T} \to \mathbb{R}$.

For each fixed regularity class $r \in [1, \infty] \cup \{\omega\}$ (where $\omega$ denotes real-analytic), does there exist an area-preserving twist map $f$ of class $C^r$ on $\mathbb{A}$ that admits a rotational invariant curve $\Gamma$ which is not of class $C^1$ (equivalently, whose graphing function $\psi$ is not continuously differentiable)?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is resolved affirmatively in low regularity: M.-C. Arnaud constructed a $C^1$ symplectic twist map with a non-differentiable essential invariant curve (2011), and Avila–Fayad (2019) extended this to a $C^1$ example with minimal dynamics on the curve. Arnaud also produced a $C^2$ example with a Denjoy-type non-differentiable invariant curve. For higher regularity classes $C^r$ with $r \geq 3$, $C^\infty$, and the real-analytic case $C^\omega$, no such examples are known and the question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A non-differentiable essential irrational invariant curve for a C^1 symplectic twist map (Arnaud)
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs a C^1 symplectic twist map of the annulus with an essential invariant curve that is not differentiable.
status_evidence.claim: The r=1 case of Mather's question has been answered affirmatively.

status_evidence.title: Non-differentiable irrational curves for C^1 twist map (Avila–Fayad)
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs a C^1 symplectic twist map having a non-differentiable essential invariant curve on which the restricted dynamics is minimal.
status_evidence.claim: Strengthens the C^1 construction with minimal dynamics on the invariant curve.

status_evidence.title: On Non-KAM Invariant Circles for Area-Preserving Twist Maps
status_evidence.snippet: Recent findings provide new evidence in support of affirmative answers to questions posed by Mather in 1998.
status_evidence.claim: Higher-regularity versions of the question remain a subject of current investigation.
